ja: 英語の breakfast は「断食（fast）を破る（break）」から。夜のあいだ食べなかった状態を終える食事という意味。
easy: 'Breakfast' means to 'break' your 'fast'. You have not eaten all night, and this meal ends that.
std: 'Breakfast' literally means breaking the fast of the night, the first meal after hours without food.

ja: company（会社・仲間）はラテン語の「com（いっしょに）＋ panis（パン）」から。もとは「いっしょにパンを食べる仲間」。
easy: The word 'company' first meant people who eat bread together.
std: 'Company' comes from Latin com, 'with', and panis, 'bread': originally, people who share bread.

ja: deadline はもともと、捕虜収容所で越えると撃たれる「死の線」を指した。今は「締め切り」の意味で使われる。
easy: 'Deadline' once meant a line in a prison camp that you must not cross. Now it means the last time to finish work.
std: 'Deadline' originally referred to a line around a prison camp that prisoners could not cross without being shot; today it means a time limit.

ja: budget（予算）は、古いフランス語の bougette（小さな革袋）から。お金を入れる袋が「予算」の意味になった。
easy: The word 'budget' comes from an old French word for a small bag for money.
std: 'Budget' comes from Old French bougette, a small leather bag, from the purse that held money.

ja: salary の語源は塩（sal）、wage は「誓い・保証」、fee は古い英語の「家畜・財産」に関係する。お金の言葉にはそれぞれ歴史がある。
easy: Many money words have long stories. 'Fee' is connected to an old word for farm animals.
std: Money words have deep roots: 'fee' is related to an old Germanic word for livestock, which once served as wealth.

ja: disaster（災害）は「dis（悪い）＋ aster（星）」から。昔の人は、悪い星の並びが不幸を招くと考えた。
easy: 'Disaster' means 'bad star'. People once thought the stars could bring bad luck.
std: 'Disaster' comes from Italian disastro, 'ill-starred', from the old belief that unlucky star positions caused misfortune.

ja: 英語の mortgage（住宅ローン）はフランス語の「死（mort）の誓い（gage）」から。借金を返し終えるか、返せなくなると誓いが「死ぬ」ため。
easy: 'Mortgage' comes from French words that mean 'death promise'. The promise ends when the loan is paid or lost.
std: 'Mortgage' comes from Old French for 'death pledge': the deal 'dies' when the debt is either repaid or the property is lost.

ja: 英語には、ある単語の中に正反対の意味を持つものがある。sanction は「認める」と「制裁」の両方を意味する。
easy: Some English words have two opposite meanings. 'Sanction' can mean 'allow' or 'punish'.
std: Some English words are their own opposites: 'sanction' can mean to approve something or to impose a penalty.

ja: 英語の単語のおよそ3割はフランス語から来たと言われる。1066年にフランスのノルマンディー公がイングランドを征服したことが大きい。
easy: Many English words come from French. This began after a French duke took over England in 1066.
std: A large share of English vocabulary comes from French, much of it after the Norman Conquest of England in 1066.

ja: 英語の pig（豚）は動物の名前で英語由来、pork（豚肉）はフランス語由来。料理を食べる上流階級がフランス語を話していた名残。
easy: 'Pig' is an old English word, but 'pork' comes from French. Rich people who ate the meat spoke French.
std: English uses native words for farm animals (pig, cow) but French-derived words for their meat (pork, beef), a legacy of Norman rule.

ja: 「ド・レ・ミ」の名前は、11世紀の修道士グイードが、聖歌の各行の最初の音節から取ってつけた。
easy: The names do, re, mi come from the first sounds of each line of an old church song.
std: The note names do, re, mi come from an 11th-century hymn: Guido of Arezzo used the first syllable of each line.

ja: 葛飾北斎の「神奈川沖浪裏」は、世界で最もよく知られた日本の絵のひとつ。ゴッホやドビュッシーにも影響を与えた。
easy: Hokusai's picture of a great wave is one of the most famous Japanese pictures in the world.
std: Hokusai's 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa' is one of the world's best-known Japanese artworks and inspired artists such as Van Gogh and composer Debussy.

ja: ジョン・ケージの曲「4分33秒」では、演奏者は楽器を弾かない。聞こえるのは会場のまわりの音だけ。
easy: In John Cage's piece '4′33″', the player does not play any notes. You only hear the sounds in the room.
std: In John Cage's 4′33″, the performer plays nothing; the music is the ambient sound of the room.

ja: ストラディバリが作ったバイオリンは今も約600台残り、1台が十数億円で取引されることもある。
easy: Violins made by Stradivari about 300 years ago can sell for many millions of dollars.
std: About 600 instruments made by Antonio Stradivari survive, and some violins have sold for over ten million dollars.

ja: ミケランジェロはシスティーナ礼拝堂の天井画を約4年かけて描いた。立ったまま上を向いて描いたと考えられている。
easy: Michelangelo spent about four years painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
std: Michelangelo spent about four years, from 1508 to 1512, painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, mostly standing and looking up.

ja: 人の耳に聞こえる音の高さは、およそ20Hzから2万Hzまで。年を重ねると高い音が聞こえにくくなる。
easy: People can hear sounds from about 20 to 20,000 vibrations a second. As we get older, we hear high sounds less well.
std: Human hearing ranges from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, and the upper limit drops with age.

ja: 近代オリンピックの第1回は1896年にアテネで開かれた。参加したのは男子選手だけだった。
easy: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896. Only men took part.
std: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, and only men competed.

ja: バレーボールは1895年、バスケットボールより激しくない室内スポーツとしてアメリカで考えられた。
easy: Volleyball was made in the US in 1895 as a softer indoor sport than basketball.
std: Volleyball was invented in 1895 in the US by William Morgan as a less intense indoor alternative to basketball.

ja: 柔道は1882年に嘉納治五郎が始めた。1964年の東京五輪で正式種目になった。
easy: Judo was started by Kano Jigoro in 1882. It became an Olympic sport at the 1964 Tokyo Games.
std: Judo was founded by Kanō Jigorō in 1882 and became an Olympic sport at the 1964 Tokyo Games.

ja: 男子100mの世界記録はウサイン・ボルトの9秒58（2009年）。最高速度は時速44km台に達したと分析されている。
easy: Usain Bolt ran 100 meters in 9.58 seconds in 2009. No one has run faster.
std: Usain Bolt's 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009, included a top speed of around 44 km per hour.

ja: 卓球は19世紀末のイギリスで、食卓の上で遊ぶ室内遊びとして始まった。ボールの音から「ピンポン」とも呼ばれた。
easy: Table tennis began in England in the 1800s as a game on a dinner table. People called it 'ping-pong' because of its sound.
std: Table tennis began in Victorian England as an after-dinner parlor game, nicknamed 'ping-pong' after the sound of the ball.

ja: 素数は無限にある。このことは2000年以上前にユークリッドが証明している。
easy: There is no biggest prime number. Euclid showed this more than 2,000 years ago.
std: There are infinitely many prime numbers, as Euclid proved more than 2,000 years ago.

ja: 1枚の紙を半分に折り続けると、厚さは折るたびに2倍になる。42回折れれば、計算上は月まで届く厚さになる。
easy: If you could fold a paper 42 times, it would be thick enough to reach the moon.
std: Because thickness doubles with every fold, a sheet of paper folded 42 times would, in theory, be thick enough to reach the Moon.

ja: 「ルービックキューブ」は、どんなに崩れた状態でも20手以内でそろえられることが2010年に証明された。
easy: Any Rubik's Cube can be solved in 20 moves or fewer. This was shown in 2010.
std: In 2010 researchers proved that every position of a Rubik's Cube can be solved in 20 moves or fewer, a number called 'God's number'.

ja: トランプ52枚をよく切ると、その並び方はほぼ確実に歴史上はじめての並びになる。並べ方は約8×10の67乗通りもある。
easy: When you mix a pack of 52 cards well, the order is almost surely new in all of history.
std: A well-shuffled deck of 52 cards is almost certainly in an order never seen before, since there are about 8 × 10^67 possible orders.

ja: 世界で最も長い川はナイル川（約6650km）とされるが、アマゾン川のほうが長いという研究もあり、議論が続いている。
easy: The Nile is often called the longest river. Some studies say the Amazon is longer.
std: The Nile, about 6,650 km, is usually called the world's longest river, though some studies argue the Amazon is longer.

ja: 死海は塩分がとても濃く、人の体は自然に浮く。湖面は海面より約430mも低い。
easy: The water in the Dead Sea is so salty that people float. It is about 430 meters below the level of the sea.
std: The Dead Sea is so salty that swimmers float easily, and its shore is about 430 meters below sea level, the lowest land on Earth.

ja: アマゾンの熱帯雨林は世界の陸上の生き物の種類の約1割がすむと言われる、生物多様性の宝庫。
easy: About one in ten known kinds of land animals and plants live in the Amazon rainforest.
std: The Amazon rainforest is home to roughly 10% of the world's known species.

ja: 琵琶湖は日本最大の湖で、数十万年以上の歴史をもつ世界有数の古い湖。
easy: Lake Biwa is the biggest lake in Japan. It is one of the oldest lakes in the world.
std: Lake Biwa, Japan's largest lake, is also one of the world's oldest lakes, hundreds of thousands of years old.

ja: QRコードは1994年に日本のデンソーウェーブが、自動車部品の管理のために開発した。
easy: The QR code was made in Japan in 1994 to keep track of car parts.
std: The QR code was invented in 1994 by Japan's Denso Wave to track automotive parts.

ja: 絵文字（emoji）は1999年ごろ日本の携帯電話向けに作られ、今では英語の辞書にも emoji として載っている。
easy: Emoji were first made for Japanese mobile phones around 1999. Now 'emoji' is an English word.
std: Emoji were created for Japanese mobile phones in the late 1990s, and the word 'emoji' is now in English dictionaries.

ja: 世界初の携帯電話による通話は1973年。端末の重さは1kg以上あった。
easy: The first mobile phone call was made in 1973. The phone weighed more than one kilogram.
std: The first handheld mobile phone call was made in 1973 by Martin Cooper of Motorola, on a phone weighing over a kilogram.

ja: 新幹線は1964年に開業した世界初の高速鉄道。長年、乗客の死亡事故ゼロを続けている。
easy: The Shinkansen started in 1964. It was the first high-speed train in the world.
std: Japan's Shinkansen, opened in 1964, was the world's first high-speed rail line and has an outstanding safety record.

ja: 「エビングハウスの忘却曲線」：覚えたことは最初の1日で大きく忘れるが、間をあけて復習すると忘れにくくなる。
easy: We forget a lot in the first day after we learn something. Reviewing at good times helps us remember.
std: Hermann Ebbinghaus found that we forget much of what we learn within a day, but spaced review slows forgetting.

ja: 「間隔反復」：同じ時間を使うなら、一度にまとめて覚えるより、日をあけて何度も復習したほうが長く覚えていられる。
easy: It is better to study a little on many days than to study a lot on one day.
std: Spaced repetition, reviewing material at growing intervals, leads to much better long-term memory than cramming.

ja: 新しい習慣が自動的になるまでの日数は人によって大きく違い、ある研究では中央値が約66日だった。
easy: A study found it takes about two months for a new habit to feel natural.
std: One study found that new habits took a median of about 66 days to become automatic, with wide variation between people.

ja: 「もし〇〇したら△△する」と決めておく if-then プランは、目標を行動に移す助けになることが多くの研究で示されている。
easy: Planning 'If this happens, then I will do that' helps people do what they want to do.
std: Research on 'implementation intentions', if-then plans, shows they help people turn goals into action.

ja: 人の体の中で一番大きい細胞は卵子、一番小さい細胞のひとつは精子。
easy: The biggest cell in the human body is the egg cell.
std: The largest cell in the human body is the egg cell, while the sperm cell is among the smallest.

ja: 胃の内側の粘膜は数日ごとに新しく入れかわり、強い胃酸から胃自身を守っている。
easy: The inside of your stomach makes a new cover every few days. This keeps strong acid from hurting it.
std: The stomach lining renews itself every few days, protecting the stomach from its own strong acid.

ja: 人は鼻をつまむと、食べ物の味の多くが分かりにくくなる。「味」と感じているものの多くは、実はにおい。
easy: If you close your nose, much food tastes less clear. A lot of what we call taste is really smell.
std: Much of what we call flavor comes from smell, which is why food tastes bland when your nose is blocked.

ja: カレーライスはインドからイギリスを経て明治時代の日本に伝わり、日本独自の料理として広まった。
easy: Curry came to Japan from India through Britain. It changed into a Japanese dish.
std: Curry reached Japan from India by way of Britain in the Meiji era and developed into a distinct Japanese dish.

ja: とうもろこしのひげ1本1本は、実の1粒1粒につながっている。
easy: Each hair on an ear of corn is connected to one corn seed.
std: Each strand of corn silk is connected to a single kernel; a kernel only develops if its strand is pollinated.
